title: High-order coefficients of sums of juntas
statement: Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose basis function is constantly one. For integers $n,k\ge 0$, suppose $f:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$ is a finite sum, over coordinate sets $J$, of functions each depending only on the coordinates in its corresponding $J$, with every term indexed by a set of size greater than $k$ equal to zero. Then the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at any multi-index whose number of nonconstant coordinates is greater than $k$ is zero.
